quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When you see this sign, you must:

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Any eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely at the intersection. Look for pedestrians and other traffic. Wait until it is safe before you go.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, you should start from:
questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: When you turn left from a multilane street or highway, start from the left lane.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require a driver to slow down and pay extra attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, like vehicles striping, mowing, or removing snow. They are marked with orange signs with black letters or symbols. Always slow down and pay close attention in work zones.

questions.question: For drivers age 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 or older cannot drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which of these is used on some highways to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows in lanes show drivers which lanes to use. They indicate whether you should drive straight or turn.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow on a traffic signal, you:

options.text: Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
May turn left after you let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
Have the right-of-way and can turn without waiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn left after you let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. However, oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians first.

questions.question: If you are in a collision, you should:

options.text: Move the injured to where they want to go.
Avoid moving the injured unless you must.
Only call for help if it seems necessary.
Tell the injured they are fine and do not need help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid moving the injured unless you must.
questions.explanation: In a collision, call emergency services right away. Do not move injured people unless it is absolutely necessary, as moving them can cause more harm.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Curve ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare you for upcoming road hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign alerts you that a curve is coming in the road.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until it passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights or a siren approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Failing to yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk may result in:

options.text: Only a fine and points on your license.
Points on your license, a fine, license suspension, community service, and jail time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Points on your license, a fine, license suspension, community service, and jail time.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. Not doing so can result in points on your license, a fine up to $500, up to 25 days in jail, required community service, and a license suspension up to six months.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Letting the car run in the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Quick stops waste fuel. You use more fuel to speed back up after braking. Drivers who look ahead can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: You can avoid a traffic signal by driving on public or private property:

options.text: If the property owner gives permission.
If a police officer tells you to.

questions.correctAnswerText: If a police officer tells you to.
questions.explanation: Driving on public or private property to avoid a traffic signal is illegal. The only exception is when a police officer directs you to do so.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines dividing the roads. You may:

options.text: Cross only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross to pass other vehicles if no traffic is coming.
Cross only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross only to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either direction. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: You should signal ____ before you begin to turn.
questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: When you meet a car with bright headlights, you should:

options.text: Use your high beams until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a car has its high beams on, look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar place, you should:

options.text: Use road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you drive.
Know only generally where you are going.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you drive.
questions.explanation: Plan your route before driving to an unfamiliar area. Check a map to find your destination before you start driving.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down but don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but don't know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop. Wait until you know it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: A red circle with a slash through it on a sign means:

options.text: Some drivers must yield to others.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash is a sign that forbids an action. These signs are rectangular with white background and red and black markings.

questions.question: Your car hits a parked car and you cannot find the owner. You must:

options.text: Leave after doing what you can.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.

questions.question: Which recommendation does not help with safe night driving?

options.text: Know that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.
Carry a flashlight in your car.
Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights hurts your vision. Your pupils shrink from the bright light. After the car passes, your eyes need time to readjust. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed to pass a stopped school bus in front of a school?
questions.correctAnswerText: 10 mph
questions.explanation: When a school bus is stopped at a school to drop off or pick up students, you can only pass it at 10 mph or slower, if it is safe. Always drive carefully near children and other pedestrians.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is coming ahead. The road will split into two one-way lanes separated by a median. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what lights should you use?

options.text: It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with no traffic control, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, look in all directions, and then go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to yield to prevent a crash. Release the gas pedal, cover the brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the hardest season to drive in.
Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid in winter.
Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
Snow tires are the best choice for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cruise control is safe to use in winter weather.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or similar bad conditions. Winter is very challenging for driving and needs extra care. Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often. Snow tires help improve grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: What driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to the vehicle for better grip.
Leave the highway as soon as possible.
Slow down and leave more space between cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and leave more space between cars.
questions.explanation: Reduce speed on snow and ice. This and increasing your following distance are the best ways to avoid crashes in these conditions.

questions.question: Your vehicle blocks traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the traveled road if possible. Never leave the accident scene without giving your information and offering help.

questions.question: An oncoming driver does not dim their high beams. Where should you look?

options.text: Toward the right side of the road
Toward the left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, look toward the right side of the road. This prevents you from being blinded and lets you see enough to stay on course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: What is the default speed limit in suburban business districts?
questions.correctAnswerText: 35 mph
questions.explanation: The default speed limit in suburban business districts is 35 mph. Follow posted signs if a different limit is shown.

questions.question: If an oncoming vehicle uses high beams, where should you look?

options.text: The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle has high beams on and does not dim them, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you see enough to stay on course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: When changing lanes to the left, where should you look to check your blind spot?
questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: Vehicles should not idle for more than:
questions.correctAnswerText: Three minutes.
questions.explanation: By law, do not let your vehicle idle for more than three minutes. Idling wastes fuel and harms the environment and your health.

questions.question: You are driving in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders for other vehicles before changing lanes.
Check your mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Always check your mirrors and use your turn signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicycle.
The cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing bicycles because a cyclist may suddenly swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road. Always drive carefully near bicyclists.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs prepare drivers for upcoming hazards. This sign warns that bicycles may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: When parallel parking, park within ____ inches of the curb.
questions.correctAnswerText: Six
questions.explanation: Your wheels should be within six inches of the curb when parallel parking. Park only where it does not block traffic and where other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement mean?

options.text: Drivers in the proper lane may make the movement indicated by the arrow, if they choose to do so.
Drivers in the proper lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow, but only if traffic lights are not working.
Drivers in the proper lane must always come to a complete stop before making the movement indicated by the arrow.
Drivers in the proper lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow while following directions indicated by traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers in the proper lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow while following directions indicated by traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the pavement shows you must move in that direction. Follow any traffic signs or signals before moving in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
The road that you are on intersects with a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road that you are on intersects with a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or barrier.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your four-way (emergency) flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map for directions.
Only if you have an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you have an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on the freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards on the road ahead?

options.text: Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
Maintain focus toward the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.
questions.explanation: Good driving depends on spotting problems early. Look far ahead and scan the entire road and sides, not just the center. This helps you handle dangerous situations safely.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight ahead.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill next to a curb, set your parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your car rolls, it will hit the curb and stop.

questions.question: A driver under 21 with a GDL permit must practice supervised driving for at least ____ before taking the road test.
questions.correctAnswerText: Six months
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 with a GDL permit must practice supervised driving for at least six months before taking the road test. Drivers 21 or older on a GDL must practice for at least three months.

questions.question: The driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. This hand signal means the driver plans to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand are extended upward, they are signaling a right turn. Adjust your driving if you see this hand signal.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic movement. They are usually white with black markings and must always be obeyed.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants toward the left. This shows that:

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will be required to turn left just ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: Edge lines mark the boundary between the travel lane and shoulder. When the edge line angles toward the center of the road, the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.question: You must turn your headlights on:

options.text: When you turn your wipers on.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use headlights from one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise. Also use them anytime you cannot see 500 feet ahead or whenever windshield wipers are on.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into:

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to your destination direction. Turn into the lane closest to your previous lane.

questions.question: When approaching a steady green arrow traffic signal, drivers:

options.text: Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.
May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
May drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane for the turn. Always yield to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.

questions.question: With a valid learner permit, you can practice driving:
questions.correctAnswerText: Between 5 a.m. and 11 p.m.
questions.explanation: With a learner permit, you cannot drive between 11:00 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.

questions.question: Pennant-shaped signs indicate:
questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zones.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. Text on the sign confirms it is a no passing area.
